title: 11 PDF Fighters Killed in Junta Ambush, Taungtha Township — Bodies Reportedly Burned; Fighters Were Traveling to Village Believing Troops Had Withdrawn
detail: Eleven People's Defence Force fighters were killed and two are missing after a junta ambush in Taungtha Township, Mandalay Region, according to Myanmar Now and The Irrawaddy reporting on May 6, 2026. The ambush occurred on approximately May 4 at the Thanbo Ma village area: 13 members of the Min Thar Gyi column of the Taungtha PDF drove toward a village after believing junta troops had withdrawn, only to find soldiers had deliberately stayed behind in a planned ambush. The vehicle column was attacked, and 11 fighters were killed. Two survivors remain unaccounted for. Junta forces reportedly burned the bodies of the fallen PDF fighters — a practice documented in previous incidents that the NUG has characterized as deliberate intimidation and desecration. Weapons seized by junta forces included 3 MA-1 rifles, 1 MA-3 rifle, one 60mm mortar, ammunition, body armor, and one vehicle. The ambush reflects the SAC's tactical shift toward counter-ambush operations using delayed-withdrawal tactics in Mandalay Region — an area that has seen sustained PDF operations including the April 28 Myingyan convoy ambush that killed ~25 SAC troops. Multiple confirmations from Myanmar Now and Irrawaddy.

media.caption: 11 Myanmar resistance PDF fighters killed in junta ambush in Taungtha Township, Mandalay Region; bodies reportedly burned — Myanmar Now, May 6, 2026

title: SAC Forces Burn 5+ Salin Township Villages, Kill 2 Elderly, Take 9 Hostages Including Novice Monk — Part of Magway Region Offensive
detail: Myanmar junta forces invaded and burned at least five villages in Salin Township, Magway Region, killing two elderly residents unable to flee and taking nine people hostage — including a novice monk — as part of a broader SAC offensive launched in late April 2026, according to Mizzima reporting on May 6, 2026. The village arson campaign in Salin follows the broader SAC ground invasion of Yinmabin, Pale, and Kani townships (Sagaing Region) launched May 1 — suggesting a coordinated multi-township offensive to clear PDF-controlled territory in the central Myanmar heartland. Salin Township (Magway Region) sits near the Sagaing-Magway border and has been a PDF operational area since 2022. The killing of elderly civilians unable to evacuate and the taking of hostages (including a religious figure) are consistent with documented junta collective punishment tactics in PDF-controlled areas across Sagaing, Magway, and Chin regions. The use of hostages as human shields has been documented in multiple prior SAC operations in Sagaing Region. Mizzima also reported on the 5th consecutive day of fighting on the Kalay-Tedim road in Chin State, where both sides sustained losses, and a Hero Guerrilla Force attack on the junta gate at Gyobinkauk in Bago Region.

media.caption: SAC forces burn villages in Salin Township, kill 2 elderly, take 9 hostages; 5th day of Kalay-Tedim road fighting — Mizzima May 6, 2026

title: Junta Reportedly Preparing Offensive on Rikhawdar — Strategic India-Border Trade Hub Held by Chin Resistance Since Nov 2023
detail: Myanmar's military junta is reportedly preparing to launch operations against Rikhawdar, a strategic trade hub on the Myanmar-India border in Chin State held by the Chin National Army (CNA) and Chinland Defence Force (CDF) since November 2023, according to DVB reporting on May 6, 2026. The expected offensive on Rikhawdar follows the SAC's April 25-26 recapture of Falam (Chin State capital) and May 5 capture of Mawlu (Sagaing Region) — indicating a broader junta strategy to roll back resistance gains in western and northwestern Myanmar and cut the resistance's connections to India's border. Rikhawdar (also spelled Rih Khua Dar or Rizua) is an important border crossing point between Chin State and Mizoram, India, and a supply conduit for Chin resistance forces. The junta has already attacked Chin State villages near the India border — including the May 1 airstrike on Khawpuichhip and Zimpi villages (5 children killed) that triggered 150+ refugees to flee into Mizoram — suggesting a pattern of preparation for deeper Chin operations. An SAC offensive on Rikhawdar would compound India's border security concerns and increase civilian refugee flows into Mizoram and Manipur. DVB's coverage tied the Rikhawdar threat directly to the broader five-year PDF anniversary context.

media.caption: Myanmar military eyes Rikhawdar India-border town in Chin State as resistance marks PDF 5th anniversary — DVB, May 6, 2026
